function: Satellite UPA 3-D beamforming: LSTM-Transformer predicts line-of-sight AOA from ephemeris; set-Transformer outputs 128 feed weights for beam and null steering (pp. 2, 7-8).
system: LEO intersatellite link, 8x8 UPA (half-wavelength spacing), elevation 0-60 deg, azimuth 0-360 deg; one desired and up to five interferers; carrier frequency not stated; no RIS (pp. 2, 6).
method: Supervised learning: LSTM-Transformer AOA predictor (about 3,300 parameters) and improved Set Transformer beamformer (about 170,000 parameters, masking, pooling); hyperparameters tuned by polar lights optimizer (pp. 7-9).
data_channel: Orbit-derived AOA series (CelesTrak TLE, SGP4; 30,000 training, 1,500 validation samples per scenario) and synthetic null-steering beamforming labels (2x10^6 samples); Saleh-Valenzuela channel formulated, datasets use angles only (pp. 4-6).
test_conditions: Predictor validated on 1,500 samples per orbit scenario; beamformer tested on 3,000 new AOA sets and 2-6 input signals; no unseen scenario or array tested (pp. 5, 11, 14).
baselines: Non-learned: null-steering beamformer (NSB). Learned: LSTM beamformer; PLO-tuned versus untuned LSTM-Transformer predictor; PLO versus GS, PSO, BO for hyperparameters (pp. 8, 10, 13).
metrics: Main lobe and null angular divergence, array factor towards desired and interfering signals, SINR, response time; predictor MAE, MAPE, RMSE, MSE, R2 (pp. 10-14).
complexity: Order O(n^3) NSB, O(n) LSTM, O(nm) SET; about 3,300 predictor and 170,000 beamformer parameters; response times 2.17 ms predictor, 1.38 ms beamformer, 53 h training (pp. 9, 11-13).
openness: none for own code or data; orbit inputs are public TLEs from CelesTrak, link given (p. 5).
q1_support: p. 4: "incorporate dynamic extensions to characterize the transmission properties" (Saleh-Valenzuela model, LOS plus NLOS). The networks are trained on orbit-derived angles and null-steering weights (pp. 5-6), not on a channel; no 3GPP model or channel measurements are used.
q2_support: p. 11: "we conducted statistical analysis using 3000 new scenarios" are fresh random AOA sets of the same generator; p. 5: "30 000 data samples for model training and 1500 samples for" validation in each of the three orbit scenarios. A held-out part of the same data does not count; no unseen scenario, band, or array is tested.
q3_support: p. 12: "the NSB algorithm and two pretrained NN beamformers" (NSB is non-learned, the second beamformer is an LSTM); p. 12: "the SET model demonstrates outstanding performance in main lobe positioning accuracy" with Table II (p. 13) comparing main lobe and null divergence and SINR of NSB, LSTM and SET.
q4_support: p. 12: "the computational complexity of NSB is" O(n^3), LSTM O(n), SET O(nm); p. 9: "with about 3,300 parameters" for the predictor and about 170,000 for the beamformer; measured response times in Table II and Table III (p. 13).
q5_support: p. 5: "we use data sourced from https:" //celestrak.org/NORAD/elements/ gives public orbital elements (TLE) only; the beamforming dataset is synthetic (2x10^6 samples, p. 6) and no code or dataset link of the authors appears anywhere in the paper.
notes: Area 6 rather than 3: beam control of a satellite UPA in LEO intersatellite links, and the more specific area wins. The AOA predictor alone would be DOA estimation (excluded), but the second network outputs the beamforming weights (p. 8), so the work passes the function check. The beamformer imitates the NSB weights (p. 6). CelesTrak TLEs are public orbital elements, not a channel or signal dataset, so q1 and q5 are 0, which the reviewer may overrule. The claim of better generalization of the LSTM-Transformer to other scenarios (p. 7) has no reported test. The 2 to 6 signal counts fall within the zero-padded set sizes used in training (p. 6). Tables I to IV and Figs. 11, 12, 17 to 19 were read as images.
